# `docker_image`

`docker_image` makes sure that the node has one Docker image, pulled from a
registry. An **image** is a packaged filesystem. Docker uses the image as
the starting filesystem for an application's **container**, the environment
where Docker runs the application. A **registry** is the server that images
are pulled from. The module runs on the node and drives the `docker` command
that is installed there.

```yaml
- docker_image:
    image: registry.example.com/audio/converter:3.1
    pull_image: when_missing
```

Use `docker_image` for a container that a systemd unit runs with
`docker run`, written with `systemd_unit` and `systemd_service` like any
other service, and for an image that a scheduled job starts later with
`docker run`. The containers of a Compose project get their images from
[`docker_compose_project`](docker_compose_project.md) itself, which pulls
them. [Run containers](../../how-to/run-containers.md)
shows both ways.

`image` is an image reference with a tag or a digest, such as
`registry.example.com/audio/converter:3.1`. A reference without either is
rejected. A reference that names no registry, such as `postgres:17.2`, means
Docker Hub. `pull_image` says whether a rerun follows a tag that its
publisher moved:
[newer images under the same tag](#newer-images-under-the-same-tag)
says what `when_missing` and `always` do, and what a dryrun asks the
registry, for both Docker modules.

`docker_image` never removes an image; see
[Clean up unused images on a timer](#clean-up-unused-images-on-a-timer).

## Set up

`docker_image` needs the `docker` command and a Docker daemon that answers.
`docker_image` does not need the Compose plugin, the extension that adds
`docker compose` to the `docker` command.
[Set up](docker_compose_project.md#set-up)
on the page of `docker_compose_project` has the node tasks that install
Docker, and says what `docker_image` and `docker_compose_project` tasks do
when Docker is missing.

## Inputs

- `image` (string; required): the image reference with a tag or a digest, such as registry.example.com/audio/converter:3.1; a reference without either is rejected
- `pull_image` (`when_missing` or `always`; required): no default; when_missing pulls only when the node does not have the image, so a rerun never follows a tag that moved; always asks the registry on every run which image the reference names now and pulls it when it differs from the node's
- `registry_username` (string; optional): with registry_password: the login for the registry named in image; a private value
- `registry_password` (string; optional): with registry_username; a private value, normally a secret; it reaches docker through a private directory under /run that the task removes, never through a command line or an account's home directory; a secret in the login does not hide the task's result: MMX shows [redacted] wherever a text of the result holds the secret

## Outputs

The node task's result holds these fields. A later node task reads them as `.node_tasks.<id>.<field>`, where `<id>` is the node task's `id`.

- `status`
- `change`
- `reason`
- `value.image_id`
- `value.previous_image_id`

## What a dryrun reports

Pulls nothing and writes no login; reports would_change for an image the node does not have; with pull_image: always it asks the registry which image the reference names now without downloading it, with the task's own login only, and reports would_change with both image IDs and, in reason, the digest under which the registry serves the image when that differs from the node's, or not_checked with the error when the registry does not answer, and then predicts no restart of a service that follows an image the node has; when the reference names a list of images for several platforms, the registry serves another list, and the node's Docker uses the classic image store, it reports not_checked and predicts no restart of a service that follows the image, because it cannot see whether the image for the node's platform changed; value.image_id is null where it is known only after the pull: on a node whose Docker uses the classic image store, and for a missing image with when_missing whose reference has a tag; not_checked while the docker command or the Docker daemon is missing.

## Retries and time limits

Bounded automatic retries by default; retry: false turns them off.

The node task takes the time limits `time_limit` and `time_limit_per_try`; without them, the project's `node_task_defaults` apply. `mmx describe-module task` describes the settings every node task accepts.

## Examples

### One image for a container that systemd runs

```yaml
- task_block:
    id: audio_converter
    changes:
      - docker_image:
          image: registry.example.com/audio/converter:3.1
          pull_image: when_missing
          registry_username: "{{ .vars.registry_username }}"
          registry_password: "{{ .secrets.registry_password }}"
      - systemd_unit:
          name: audio-converter.service
          content: |
            [Unit]
            Requires=docker.service
            After=docker.service
            [Service]
            ExecStartPre=-/usr/bin/docker rm --force audio-converter
            ExecStart=/usr/bin/docker run --rm --name audio-converter registry.example.com/audio/converter:3.1
            ExecStop=/usr/bin/docker stop audio-converter
            Restart=always
            [Install]
            WantedBy=multi-user.target
    activate:
      - systemd_service:
          name: audio-converter
          state: running
          start_at_boot: true
```

On the node, MMX first pulls the image if the node lacks the image, using
the login for `registry.example.com`. The `systemd_unit` task installs
`audio-converter.service`, and the `systemd_service` task starts and enables
it. When a later run pulls an image with another ID, the `systemd_service`
task restarts the service; [How it works](#how-it-works) says why. To wait
until the container's own health check reports healthy, add a `wait_for` task
with `docker_container_is_healthy: audio-converter` in `verify`; see
[Wait until a container is healthy](docker_compose_project.md#wait-until-a-container-is-healthy).

The login reaches Docker without a password on a command line, in an
account's home directory, or on a disk;
[logins for private registries](../../how-to/run-containers.md#pull-from-a-private-registry)
says how.

### Clean up unused images on a timer

Old images fill the disk. MMX deletes none by itself. A
[`docker_unused_images`](docker_unused_images.md) node task deletes unused
images once, such as in a one-time playbook. A timer deletes unused images
on a schedule:

```yaml
- task_block:
    id: docker_image_cleanup
    changes:
      - systemd_unit:
          name: docker-image-cleanup.service
          content: |
            [Service]
            Type=oneshot
            ExecStart=/usr/bin/docker image prune --all --force --filter until=168h
      - systemd_unit:
          name: docker-image-cleanup.timer
          content: |
            [Timer]
            OnCalendar=Sun 04:00
            Persistent=true
            [Install]
            WantedBy=timers.target
    activate:
      - systemd_service:
          name: docker-image-cleanup.timer
          state: running
          start_at_boot: true
```

Every Sunday at 04:00 the node deletes the images that no container uses and
that are older than seven days. Docker's **image stores** are the systems
Docker uses to keep images on the node: classic and containerd.
With Docker's classic image store, the seven days count from when the image
was built. With the containerd image store, which a new installation of
Docker 29 uses, an image that came onto the node
within the last seven days stays, however long ago it was built.

## How it works

The task is unchanged when the node has the image and, with `always`, the
registry still names the same image for the reference. Its result has
`value.image_id` and `value.previous_image_id`, which is null when the node
did not have the image. They are the IDs that `docker image inspect` reports
on the node.

In the `changes` of a node task block, the image ID is a
[tracked input](shell.md#commands-that-follow-tracked-inputs) of the
block, like the version of an installed package: the `systemd_service` task
in `activate` restarts the service when the image ID differs from the one the
service last started with. That also holds when the run that pulled the
image stopped before the restart: the next run finds the image unchanged and
still restarts the service once. A dryrun predicts the restart.

### Newer images under the same tag

An **image** is the packaged filesystem a container starts from. A
**registry** is the server that images are pulled from. An image reference
such as `registry.example.com/shop/web:2.4` names the registry, the image,
and a **tag**. Whoever publishes an image can move a tag to a newer image; a
**digest** (`@sha256:...`) names exactly one image forever.

Most projects name an image by a tag that its publisher moves, such as
`latest` or `17`. Whether a rerun deploys the newer image is a required
choice on the task, `pull_image` on `docker_image` and `pull_images` on
[`docker_compose_project`](docker_compose_project.md):

- `when_missing` pulls an image only when the node does not have it. A rerun
  never replaces a running container because a tag moved. Use `when_missing`
  with tags that name one version, and with digests.
- `always` asks the registry on every run which image each reference names
  now, pulls an image that differs from the node's, and recreates the
  containers of that image. The task reports changed and lists each pulled
  image with its previous and its new image ID.

With `always`, an unchanged project and an unchanged registry give an
unchanged rerun.

A dryrun with `always` asks the registry the same question without
downloading the image. When the registry names another image than the node
has, the dryrun reports `would_change`, the service it would recreate, and
the image with `previous_image_id` and `image_id`. When the registry does not
answer, the task reports `not_checked` with the error, and a `docker_image`
task predicts no restart of a service that follows an image the node has. A
dryrun with `when_missing` reports `would_change` only for an image the node
does not have.

**An image for several platforms.** Most public images, Docker's official
images among them, are a list of images under one tag: one image for each
platform, such as `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. The registry's answer
names the list. The list changes whenever the image for any platform is
rebuilt, and the answer does not say whether the image for this node's
platform is among them. So when the registry serves another list than the
node's image came from, a dryrun does not claim what it cannot see:

- A service of a Compose project that uses the image, and whose container
  already exists, reports the action `not_checked`, with a reason that says
  so.
- With the classic image store, the pull may change nothing on the node. The
  image's entry in `value.images` then has a null `image_id` and a `reason`,
  and a `docker_image` task for an image the node has reports `not_checked`
  and predicts no restart of a service that follows it. With the containerd
  image store, the image ID is the list's digest, so the dryrun reports the
  new ID.
- The task reports `would_change` when something else in it is certain to
  change, and `not_checked` otherwise.

A run pulls. With the classic image store, the image and the containers
change only if the image for the node's platform changed. With the containerd
image store, the image gets the new ID, and Compose decides about the
containers: Compose 5 keeps a container when the image for the container's
platform has not changed. Compose 2.40 recreates a container even when the
image for the container's platform has not changed. A reference that names
one image has no such doubt: another digest is another image. To deploy
exactly what you tested, name the image by its digest.

**The image ID.** `image_id` and `previous_image_id` are the IDs that
`docker image inspect` reports on the node. The two image stores name an
image differently. The containerd image store, which a new installation of
Docker 29 uses, names it by the digest of its manifest, the digest under
which a registry serves it. The classic store, which older versions and
upgraded installations use, names it by the digest of the image's
configuration.

**What a dryrun knows of an image it would pull.** With the containerd image
store, the new image ID is the digest under which the registry serves the
image, so the dryrun reports it. With the classic store, Docker learns the ID
only with the pull: `image_id` is null in the dryrun, the task's `reason`
names the registry's digest, and a later node task that reads
`value.image_id` of a `docker_image` task is not checked. With
`when_missing`, a dryrun does not ask the registry, and `image_id` of an
image it would pull is null too. The exception is a reference with a digest
on a node with the containerd image store: the digest is the image ID, so
the dryrun reports it without asking the registry.

**How MMX asks the registry.** A dryrun asks the Docker daemon on its Unix
socket which image a reference names (`GET /distribution/<reference>/json`,
the request `docker pull` starts with). The daemon asks the registry with its
own settings: which registries it trusts without TLS, their certificates, and
its proxy. The daemon downloads no image layer. A run asks nobody
beforehand: `docker pull`, or `docker compose up --pull always`, pulls what
differs.

**Logins in a dryrun.** A dryrun asks with the task's own login only; a
login saved on the node with `docker login` does not count. For a private
image without a login on the task, the dryrun reports `not_checked` with the
registry's refusal, and the reason says that `registry_username` and
`registry_password` (`registry_logins` for a Compose project) on the task let
the dryrun check.

Modules that rely on this section: `docker_image` and
[`docker_compose_project`](docker_compose_project.md#follow-newer-images-and-pull-from-a-private-registry).

## Errors and what they mean

Every reason starts with `docker_image`.

| The reason holds | What the reason means, and what to do |
|---|---|
| `the program docker is not installed`, `the Docker daemon does not answer (...)` | Docker is missing or not started. The task is not tried again; a dryrun reports the `docker_image` task `not_checked`. See [Set up](docker_compose_project.md#set-up). |
| `docker_image needs pull_image: when_missing or always` | `pull_image` has no default. Set `pull_image` to `when_missing` or `always`. |
| `set registry_username and registry_password together, or omit registry_username and registry_password` | The task has only `registry_username` or only `registry_password`. Write `registry_username` and `registry_password` together, or omit `registry_username` and `registry_password`. |
| `docker pull ... succeeded, but Docker still reports no image under the requested reference` | Docker reported success and has no image under the reference. Check the reference with `docker image ls` on the node. |
| In a dryrun: `the docker command reaches the Docker daemon at ...; MMX can ask a registry without downloading only through a Docker daemon on a Unix socket on the node` | The `docker` command uses a daemon on another address, such as a TCP address. A dryrun with `pull_image: always` cannot ask the registry. |

## Tested on

**Distributions:** Debian 12 and 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, Rocky Linux 9, AlmaLinux 10.

The suite `tests/integration/docker_containers.py` covers `docker_image`
together with `docker_compose_project`, on the distributions and Docker
versions that the [page of `docker_compose_project`](docker_compose_project.md#tested-on)
lists.

## Why it works this way

- **`pull_image` has no default.** The choice decides whether a rerun
  deploys new software, so it must be on the page.
- **`docker_image` deletes no image.** Deleting is a separate, explicit
  node task, [`docker_unused_images`](docker_unused_images.md), or a
  schedule, not a side effect of a run. An image that a rollback needs tomorrow must not
  vanish because today's run no longer names it.
